clue.text: Negative comment that produces ill-feeling

definitions.meaning: a grumble or objection voiced about something
read literally, a feeling of being ill, an ailment or disorder

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' looks like resentment, but here it is a physical malady; 'that produces' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a grievance expressed aloud and a medical disorder, as in a liver ailment.

clue.text: Half-hearted lawman who deals with Arabs and others?

definitions.text: who deals with Arabs and others?

indicators.note: losing half of its heart means one of the two central doubled letters is dropped

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A lukewarm police officer seems to be involved in trade with Arab nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabs' are not people but horses; a coper is an old word for a horse dealer, and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A coper is a dealer in horses, and Arabs are a well-known breed of horse.

clue.text: NB, request for assessment of essay

definitions.meaning: nota bene, a warning to take note of what follows
a student literally asking a teacher to grade the piece of writing

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a stock way of saying 'heed this', and also, read literally, a plea to have one's writing graded.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are an idiomatic warning to take heed and a literal plea for grading of written work.

clue.text: Distribute information in small part of plant

definitions.meaning: to hand out printed sheets to the public, used as a verb
a tiny division of a compound plant leaf

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link between the verb sense and the botanical noun sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means hand out printed sheets; as a noun it is a small subdivision of a leaf.

clue.text: Our silly manoeuvring may be deceptive

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things about, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some foolish tactical move of ours could be misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvring' rearranges OUR SILLY; 'may be' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory gives a false impression, which is exactly what deceptive things do.

clue.text: Finishes off honest opponent not learning lesson

indicators.note: taking the finishes off means each of the two words loses its final letter

parts.note: honest means true
anti is a word for someone who opposes

explanation.surface: Someone truthful finishes off a rival while skipping class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishes off' trims the last letter from both TRUE and ANTI, leaving TRU and ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a pupil absent from school without leave, so not learning the lesson.

clue.text: Infant king rejected grilled food

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a babe is an infant
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A baby monarch turned down some barbecued dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the whole of BABE + K backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is meat cooked on a skewer over a grill, a familiar grilled dish.

clue.text: Bird damaging trees caught by characters following Juliet

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Juliet is J in the radio alphabet, and the letters after J are K and L

indicators.note: damaging the word knocks its letters out of order

explanation.surface: A bird is harming trees after being trapped by people who follow Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are alphabet letters, not people: Juliet is J in the radio alphabet, so the two that follow it hold the scrambled trees between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon, a type of bird of prey.

clue.text: Snake runs away from wild animal

indicators.note: something going away from the word is removed from it

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A snake escapes from a ferocious beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs away from' removes R (cricket's abbreviation for runs) from BOAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a large constricting snake.

clue.text: Musical group's cheap alternative to gold ring

definitions.meaning: an ensemble of trumpets, cornets and tubas
a hoop made of brass, a cheap metal resembling gold

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an ensemble of brass instruments and, read literally, a ring of brass rather than gold.

clue.text: Parents on opposite sides of river in Italian city

indicators.note: standing on either side of means the other piece is placed between them

parts.note: pa and ma are informal words for father and mother

explanation.surface: Mum and dad stand on different banks of a river in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: PA and MA go on either side of R.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in northern Italy, famous for its ham and cheese.

clue.text: Article on developing oil in USA in one state

indicators.note: on means placed after, as the final piece comes after the rest in an across entry
developing means changing form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news article about oil development within one state of the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developing' rearranges OIL IN USA, with A after it; the second 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the fifty United States, on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: They emerged from the pack as urban developers

definitions.text: They emerged from the pack as urban developers

parts.words: They emerged from the pack as urban developers
parts.note: legendary twins suckled by a she-wolf, so brought up in a wolf pack, who went on to found a great city

explanation.walkthrough: 'The pack' sounds like a group of rivals or a card deck, but it is a wolf pack; the 'urban developers' founded Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend these twins were raised by a she-wolf and founded the city of Rome.

clue.text: Disorganized bunch in shifting alliances with me

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muddled group of people in changing coalitions, including me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifting' rearranges ALLIANCES plus ME; 'with' joins them and 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellanea are a mixed assortment of items, a disorganized collection.

clue.text: Decline in business coming as sad shock

parts.note: down means low in spirits
a turn is a sudden fright, as in 'gave me a turn'

explanation.surface: A slump in trade arrives as an unhappy surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A turn' is a British idiom for a shock or scare; 'coming as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a decline in economic activity or trade.

clue.text: Protest about indecent form of government

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
C is short for circa, meaning about
racy means risqué or indecent

explanation.surface: A protest is staged over an obscene style of rule.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) stands for 'about' here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Democracy is a system of government by elected representatives of the people.

clue.text: Seek answer about 10 in another state

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: seek means ask for
the state at 10-across has the postal abbreviation LA

explanation.surface: Look for an answer to 10 in a different state.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' points to 10-across, whose abbreviation LA is put inside ASK A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is a different US state from the one at 10-across.

clue.text: Port wine

definitions.meaning: a harbour city on France's Atlantic side
the red or white produced around that city

explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the fortified wine, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is both a French port city and the wine made in the surrounding region.

clue.text: Initially mother orders pink and blue

indicators.note: initially means taking the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: rose is a shade of pink

explanation.surface: Mum chooses colours, pink and blue at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour beside 'pink', but it is the definition: sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blue means feeling low, which is what morose means, sullen and gloomy.

clue.text: Person helping to present acts -how many?

indicators.note: the run of letters spanning these words helps present the answer, so it lies within them

explanation.surface: Someone presenting circus acts asks how many there are.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'actS HOW MANy'; the surface image of a ringmaster counting turns is itself a showman.
explanation.definitionFit: A showman is a person who stages entertainments, so a person in the general sense.

clue.text: A lot of wine that's often put into trough

definitions.meaning: a large cask holding a big quantity of wine
read as a pig's head, which goes into the feeding trough

explanation.walkthrough: Split as hog's head, it is literally the pig's head dipped in the trough.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask of wine or beer, and read in two words a pig's head.

clue.text: Venomous creature unnamed in sign?

indicators.note: without a name means N, short for name, is taken out

parts.note: a scorpion is a stinging arachnid

explanation.surface: A poisonous animal unidentified in a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a standard abbreviation for name, so 'unnamed' drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is a zodiac sign, the scorpion; the question mark flags that sign means star sign.

clue.text: Ignore candidate's achievement at university

parts.note: an exam candidate achieves a pass
up means in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Overlooking what a student achieved while at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' for being at university is British usage, chiefly of Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an opportunity is to ignore or decline it.

clue.text: Stars who travelled with a golden retriever

definitions.meaning: the twin bright stars in Gemini

definitions.text: who travelled with a golden retriever
definitions.meaning: the twin Argonauts who sailed with Jason, who went to fetch the Golden Fleece

explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden retriever' sounds like a dog, but it is Jason retrieving the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the two brightest stars in Gemini, named after the twin heroes who sailed on the Argo.

clue.text: People in old South Africa finding times hard, originally

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils

indicators.note: originally means taking the first letter of each of those three words

explanation.surface: A people in historic South Africa having a tough time at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not an era but the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: The Xhosa are a Bantu people of South Africa.

clue.text: Flower I aim to replace with aster

indicators.note: replacing means putting things back in different places, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: I intend to swap one bloom for an aster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To replace' rearranges I AIM and ASTER together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a plant genus including wormwood and mugwort, some grown as garden flowers.

clue.text: Male leader of undistinguished trio

definitions.meaning: a male animal, especially a cat
the first of '..., Dick and Harry', a phrase for ordinary people

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom, Dick and Harry' is a set phrase for any ordinary people, and Tom comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, and Tom heads the phrase for anyone at all.

clue.text: Player of pipes closed festive entertainment

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god who plays panpipes
to describes a door pushed shut, as in 'pull the door to'

explanation.surface: A piper shut down the holiday show.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is a traditional British Christmas theatre show, so festive entertainment.

clue.text: State of the old people

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
men means people

explanation.surface: The condition of the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a condition, but it is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a state, a country in the south of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Supporting chap about a vote leading to a period of stability

indicators.note: leading to means coming before, so the next piece follows
about means around, so the first pieces surround the second

parts.note: pro means in favour of
taken as written
X is the mark made on a ballot paper
a man is a chap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A backer of a man about a ballot that brings a stable era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the supporter-and-chap pair around the vote, and 'leading to' adds the final letter; X is the cross a voter marks on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pax Romana was the long era of peace under the Roman Empire, a period of stability.
